messages:
Maya Thompson: Quick design check — axis tick abbrev + smoothing look off when there are intermittent spikes. Labels read 0, 5K, 10K but chart line is flat near 200. Feels misleading.
Julian Park: Saw this on the infra dashboard. Smoothing (EMA) hides short-lived spikes, but the tick scale still stretches for a single outlier.
Katherine Li: Two ideas: (1) show secondary micro-ticks for typical range (faded), (2) add an 'outlier fade' overlay that dims values outside percentile X. Both should be opt-in per-panel.
Maya Thompson: Agree. UX: micro-ticks use muted color + tooltip that says e.g. "typical range (5th-95th)". For outlier fade we need legend affordance so users know some points were de-emphasized.
Julian Park: Implementation note: we must not alter raw data on hover/CSV export. Any visual clamp/fade should be purely presentational and emit an annotation in the chart meta.
Katherine Li: Sketch of config (for devs):
```
chart.options = {
  smoothing: {method: "ema", window: 5},
  outlierPolicy: {mode: "fade", percentile: 95, showBadge: true}
}
```
Maya Thompson: Accessibility: contrast-bot flagged muted micro-ticks as low-contrast. If we use lighter strokes, ensure a11y token fallback for high-contrast mode.
contrast-bot: Automated check: micro-tick color #BFC7CC fails AA on light bg. Recommend #9EA7AE or increase stroke to 1.5px.
Julian Park: For copy in the legend badge: "De-emphasized extremes — hover for raw values". Keep it short.
Katherine Li: Acceptance criteria for RFC: clear micro-ticks for typical range, togglable outlier fade with legend badge + annotation, no change to exported/raw values, a11y token fallback. I'll mock the badge and micro-tick states.
Maya Thompson: Thanks — ping me for copy tweaks. :thumbsup:
